question.text: If the Market-Cap-to-GDP ratio of an equity market is 70%, per the workbook's textbook interpretation, the market is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's interpretation table places below 50% as Undervalued, 50% to 75% as Moderately Undervalued, 75% to 90% as Fairly Valued, 90% to 110% as Moderately Overvalued, and above 110% as Overvalued. 70% therefore falls in the Moderately Undervalued band. The Trap: 'Fairly Valued' is the adjacent band (75% to 90%) — an off-by-one bucket error. 'Undervalued' applies only below 50%, and 'Significantly Overvalued' is well outside this reading. Note: The Market-Cap-to-GDP ratio is presented as a guideline rather than a precise trigger and should be read alongside macro and interest-rate context.
